newsitem.title: USA: Sacramento, Calif., to negotiate new arena plan.
newsitem.headline: Sacramento, Calif., to negotiate new arena plan.

text.p: Sacramento, Calif., city officials and the owner of the Kings basketball team have agreed to try to develop a new proposal to help the team without tapping into the city's general fund, a city official said on Wednesday.

Earlier this month, Sacramento Kings owner Jim Thomas asked the city to help him pay off his debt at the Arco Arena and to help build a new sports and entertainment complex. Without a financial commitment from city officials, he warned that he might be forced to move the team to another city.
But Sacramento Mayor Joe Serna Jr. convinced Thomas to reconsider his proposal, according to Serna's chief of staff.
"The concern was that the city wasn't adequately protected," Chief of Staff Michael Picker said.
Thomas agreed to temporarily withdraw his proposal, and to spend a week negotiating with the city in hope of reaching a compromise.
Picker said Thomas and the city officials would try to reach agreement on a package that would help the team while insulating the city's general fund.
To aid the team, Picker said a ticket surcharge and other special fees would be considered.

Thomas had sought about $150 million from the city -- $60 million to pay off his debt at Arco Arena and about $90 million to help build a sports and entertainment complex adjacent to the nine-year-old arena.
